subject: name of encoding of intensities for readUnits

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: name of encoding of intensities for readUnits
parts:
Hi,
For different objects, the readUnits(this) will give a different name
for the intensities/stdevs/pixel part of the CEL file (e.g. 'eps' for
residuals, 'phi' for probe affinities, etc) -- as well as not return
all of them depending on the object. I know this is part of the encode
function defined under getXXX(). Is there a function that will return
this information? (so that if you make a function that does something
on CEL files and uses the readUnits() function, you don't have to
specify different methods for the probe or chip files, but rather just
have a getEncoding(this) to find it)

Thanks,
Elizabeth

Hypothetical example:
pb<-getProbeAffinities(plm)
getEncoding(pb)
[1] "phi" "sdPhi" "phiOutliers"

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] name of encoding of intensities for readUnits
parts:
On 3/23/07, epurdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
> For different objects, the readUnits(this) will give a different name
> for the intensities/stdevs/pixel part of the CEL file (e.g. 'eps' for
> residuals, 'phi' for probe affinities, etc) -- as well as not return
> all of them depending on the object. I know this is part of the encode
> function defined under getXXX().

First, the reason for having encoding and decoding functions is that
we decided to store as much as possible in binary CEL files and
utilize the affxparser I/O to read and update the values. This way we
also avoided defining yet another file format, which there are too
many of anyway. Binary CEL files store the tuple (intensity, stddev,
pixel) [float,float,integer] for each cell, but by encoding and
decoding data these 10 bytes in total can be used for other things.
Indeed, the encoding and decoding is done at the *unit group* level,
so we can encode/decode data for all cells in one unit group however
we want, which gives further flexibility. See for instance MbeiPlm;
there we encode phi, sdPhi, phiOutliers, nbrOfIterations, converged,
and convergedOutliers in each unit group by using all bits in the
bytes.

> Is there a function that will return
> this information? (so that if you make a function that does something
> on CEL files and uses the readUnits() function, you don't have to
> specify different methods for the probe or chip files, but rather just
> have a getEncoding(this) to find it)

As you've notices, in for instance getProbeAffinities() of RmaPlm the
encode and decode functions are set internally by setEncodeFunction()
and setDecodeFunction(). These are available in the ProbeAffinityFile
object as object fields. Indeed, all classes inheriting from
ParameterCelFile has decode and encode functions. The current design
is to keep this functionality very much private/protected, because I
wanted to keep it for changes. However, you can get them as
pb$encodeFunction and pb$decodeFunction.

>
> Thanks,
> Elizabeth
>
> Hypothetical example:
> pb<-getProbeAffinities(plm)
> getEncoding(pb)
> [1] "phi" "sdPhi" "phiOutliers"

This example assumes that there is one element per CEL field, which is
not the case as the MbeiPlm example illustrates. But, as is, it make
sense to bring up the encoding/decoding to the devel API (absolutely
not the user API).

Another problem, which I totally ignored but which is a problem, is
that if you don't get the ProbeAffinityFile via the ProbeLevelModel
object, but directly from the file, the encoding functions are not
set. This is because there is no information in the file on what PLM
was used. This information is only in your scripts (and in some sense
in the data set tags). Again, have though about storing this
information to file too, but since I don't want invent new file
formats this has not been done. The CEL header could be utilized, but
it is hard to update a CEL header as soon as the file is created, and
again, it requires some formal definition of the header format,
something which I did not prioritize.

As I always say, thoughs/feedback/code is appreciated.

Cheers

Henrik
